JEE-CHEM-1457 · Class XI · Medium

Newman projection and conformational change

Keep the front carbon fixed. Starting from the Newman projection shown, rotate the rear carbon clockwise through 120° as viewed. Which conformation results, and how does its energy compare with the starting conformation in the usual butane torsional-energy model?

  1. A Anti; lower energy than the starting gauche conformation
  2. B Fully eclipsed methyl groups; higher energy
  3. C Gauche; the same energy as the starting conformation
  4. D Hydrogen-eclipsed; higher energy
Answer and explanation

A. Anti; lower energy than the starting gauche conformation

The front methyl points upward and the rear methyl is 60° clockwise from it, so the starting form is gauche. Rotating the rear carbon a further 120° clockwise makes the methyl dihedral 180°: anti. Anti is lower in energy than gauche for butane.

JEE-CHEM-1458 · Class XI · Medium

Sawhorse projection and torsional strain

Read the sawhorse projection shown. Keeping the front carbon fixed, rotate the rear carbon by 60° about the C–C bond. Which change occurs in the usual ethane torsional-energy model?

  1. A Staggered to eclipsed; torsional strain increases
  2. B Eclipsed to eclipsed; torsional strain is unchanged
  3. C Eclipsed to staggered; torsional strain decreases
  4. D Staggered to staggered; three C–H bonds break
Answer and explanation

C. Eclipsed to staggered; torsional strain decreases

The parallel corresponding bonds depict eclipsed ethane: three aligned C–H bond pairs. A 60° rotation places the rear bonds between the front bonds, producing the staggered form and lowering torsional strain. No bonds break.

  2. B 4 mol

  4. D for simple alkyl carbanions the usual order is methyl greater than primary greater than secondary greater than tertiary
Answer and explanation

Carbanion stability is for simple alkyl carbanions the usual order is methyl greater than primary greater than secondary greater than tertiary. Electron-donating alkyl groups destabilize negative charge.

JEE-CHEM-1497 · Class XI · Difficult

Formula and unsaturation inference

A hydrocarbon has molar mass 56 g mol⁻¹ and carbon mass percentage 85.71429%. Its structure contains no rings. On complete catalytic hydrogenation all multiple bonds are saturated, without C–C cleavage. What amount of H₂ is consumed per mole of hydrocarbon? Use C=12, H=1. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 3 mol
  2. B 2 mol
  3. C 1 mol
  4. D 0 mol
Answer and explanation

C. 1 mol

Carbon atoms per molecule=(carbon fraction×M)/12=4; H atoms=M−12×4=8. Acyclic saturated formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so the hydrogen deficit is 2; each H₂ fills two missing H atoms. Consumption=1 mol H₂ per mole.

  2. B 0.14 g
  3. C 0.07 g
  4. D 0.28 g
Answer and explanation

B. 0.14 g

The saturated monoamine formula CnH2n+3N loses two H for the C=C, giving C6H13N, M=99. One N per molecule produces half a mole N₂ per mole, so mass=0.14 g.

A neutral acyclic hydrocarbon has formula C10H20 and contains no triple bond. How many moles H₂ are needed for complete hydrogenation of 1.06 g? C=12, H=1. Choose the closest listed value.

  2. B 0.0075714286 mol
  3. C 0.0025238095 mol
  4. D 0.0037857143 mol
Answer and explanation

B. 0.0075714286 mol

The hydrogen deficit from CnH2n+2 is 2, so there are 1 C=C bonds. Each needs one H₂; n(H₂)=1.06/(140)×1=0.0075714286 mol.

  4. D position isomerism

  2. B rotation about a sigma bond
  3. C hydrogen bonding between molecules
  4. D permanent displacement of a sigma-electron pair that occurs without an attacking reagent
Answer and explanation

A. temporary complete transfer of a pi-electron pair under an attacking reagent

The defining electron displacement is stated in the correct option.

What mass of one specified stereoisomer could be isolated by perfect separation? Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.17083333 g
  2. B 0.25625 g
  3. C 0.5125 g
  4. D 4.1 g
Answer and explanation

Without internal symmetry there are 2^4=16 stereoisomers of equal molar mass. Equal amounts divide the mass equally; one contributes 8.2/16=0.5125 g.

  4. D for simple alkyl carbanions the usual order is methyl greater than primary greater than secondary greater than tertiary

Resonance effect is electron delocalization through overlapping p orbitals. It can stabilize conjugated ions and molecules.

  4. D 75.555556 %

A. 50.37037 %

Alkyne=x, alkene=y. Hydrogen balance: 2x+y=0.0203; mass: 166x+168y=2.2544. Eliminate y: x=(168×0.0203−2.2544)/170=0.0068 mol. Then y=0.0067, giving 50.37037%.

JEE-CHEM-1633 · Class XI · Easy

general concepts

Which statement about terminal alkynes is correct?

  1. A Alkenes are more acidic because sp² has greater s-character than sp.
  2. B The acetylide ion is destabilised by greater s-character.
  3. C A terminal alkyne has an acidic hydrogen attached to an sp-hybridised carbon.
  4. D Every internal alkyne has two terminal hydrogens.
Answer and explanation

C. A terminal alkyne has an acidic hydrogen attached to an sp-hybridised carbon.

The sp orbital has 50% s-character and stabilises the conjugate base.

  2. B ozonolysis
  3. C Wurtz reaction
  4. D Markovnikov rule
Answer and explanation

C. Wurtz reaction

The defining statement matches Wurtz reaction. In addition, it is most suitable for symmetrical alkanes with even carbon count.

JEE-CHEM-1674 · Class XI · Easy

Peroxide selectivity

  1. A HBr
  2. B HCl only
  3. C HI only
  4. D All three equally
Answer and explanation

A. HBr

The radical propagation energetics support the peroxide effect for HBr under the usual conditions.

JEE-CHEM-1675 · Class XI · Easy

Ethane conformation

Looking along the C–C bond of ethane, its staggered conformation differs from the eclipsed conformation by:

  1. A A 180° change in carbon hybridisation
  2. B A change from a C–C single to double bond
  3. C Breaking one C–H bond
  4. D A 60° dihedral angle between nearest front and rear C–H bonds
Answer and explanation

D. A 60° dihedral angle between nearest front and rear C–H bonds

Rotation about C–C produces conformers; staggered nearest front/rear bonds have a 60° dihedral angle.

  1. A 5.6 mmol
  2. B 11.013953 mmol
  3. C 16.8 mmol
  4. D 5.972093 mmol
Answer and explanation

A. 5.6 mmol

Each alkene consumes one Br₂ and each diene two. Thus x+2y=0.008, and 84x+82y=0.4656. Therefore y=(84×0.008−0.4656)/(86)=0.0024 mol and x=0.0032 mol. Total=5.6 mmol.

JEE-CHEM-1681 · Class XI · Medium

Directing effect of nitro

Nitrobenzene undergoes ring chlorination under suitable Cl₂/FeCl₃ conditions. Which combination is expected?

  1. A Predominantly ortho substitution; nitro strongly activates
  2. B Predominantly meta substitution; the nitro group deactivates the ring
  3. C Predominantly para substitution; nitro donates strongly by resonance
  4. D Substitution only on nitrogen; ring aromaticity is permanently lost
Answer and explanation

B. Predominantly meta substitution; the nitro group deactivates the ring

The −I/−M nitro group deactivates the ring and destabilises the ortho/para σ-complexes more strongly, favouring meta substitution.

JEE-CHEM-1712 · Class XII · Difficult

Competing substitution pathways

Two independent substrates A and B undergo SN1 solvolysis with first-order constants k_A and k_B. Initially [A]=0.022 M and [B]=0.044 M; the total initial product-formation rate is 0.1232 M min⁻¹. A separate experiment with concentrations 3[A] and [B]/2 gives rate 0.1276 M min⁻¹. No products interconvert. Find k_A/k_B. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 1.0909091
  2. B 3.3846154
  3. C 1.6363636
  4. D 0.54545455
Answer and explanation

D. 0.54545455

The two rates are k_A[A]+k_B[B]=r₁ and 3k_A[A]+k_B[B]/2=r₂. Therefore k_A[A]=(r₂−r₁/2)/2.5=0.0264, and k_B[B]=0.0968. Dividing by the respective concentrations gives k_A/k_B=0.5454545.

JEE-CHEM-1716 · Class XII · Easy

geminal dihalide

Which description best explains Geminal dihalide?

  1. A carbocation stability controls the ionization step
  2. B a dihalide with both halogens on the same carbon
  3. C steric crowding slows the reaction
  4. D partial or substantial racemization can result

JEE-CHEM-1810 · Class XII · Difficult

Alcohol identification by quantitative tests

A 0.4856 g mixture contains only ethanol (46 g mol⁻¹) and propan-2-ol (60 g mol⁻¹). Under excess I₂/NaOH, each gives one mole of iodoform per mole of alcohol and the total iodoform obtained is 0.0094 mol. What mass of propan-2-ol was in the mixture? Choose the closest listed value.

  3. C 0.076 g
  4. D 0.228 g

D. 0.228 g

Both alcohols give the iodoform test: x+y=0.0094. Their mass balance is 46x+60y=0.4856. Subtraction gives y=(mass−46×iodoform moles)/14=0.0038 mol, hence 0.228 g propan-2-ol.

JEE-CHEM-1841 · Class XII · Difficult

Alcohol identification by quantitative tests

A 0.4248 g mixture contains only ethanol (46 g mol⁻¹) and propan-2-ol (60 g mol⁻¹). Under excess I₂/NaOH, each gives one mole of iodoform per mole of alcohol and the total iodoform obtained is 0.0082 mol. What mass of propan-2-ol was in the mixture? Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.204 g
  2. B 2.0245714 g
  3. C 1.2817143 g
  4. D 0.068 g
Answer and explanation

A. 0.204 g

Both alcohols give the iodoform test: x+y=0.0082. Their mass balance is 46x+60y=0.4248. Subtraction gives y=(mass−46×iodoform moles)/14=0.0034 mol, hence 0.204 g propan-2-ol.

JEE-CHEM-1882 · Class XII · Medium

Selective ether cleavage

Anisole is heated with excess concentrated HI. Which bond cleavage and aromatic product are expected in the usual reaction?

  2. B Both bonds remain intact; benzoic acid
  3. C Direct ring iodination alone; nitrobenzene
  4. D Cleavage of the aryl–O bond by ordinary SN2; benzene
Answer and explanation

A. Cleavage at the methyl–O bond; phenol

Iodide attacks the methyl carbon; the aryl carbon is unsuitable for ordinary backside SN2 displacement. Phenol is the aromatic product.

JEE-CHEM-1884 · Class XII · Difficult

Alcohol identification by quantitative tests

A 0.44 g mixture contains only ethanol (46 g mol⁻¹) and propan-2-ol (60 g mol⁻¹). Under excess I₂/NaOH, each gives one mole of iodoform per mole of alcohol and the total iodoform obtained is 0.0085 mol. What mass of propan-2-ol was in the mixture? Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.21 g
  2. B 2.0957143 g
  3. C 0.42 g
  4. D 0.63 g
Answer and explanation

A. 0.21 g

Both alcohols give the iodoform test: x+y=0.0085. Their mass balance is 46x+60y=0.44. Subtraction gives y=(mass−46×iodoform moles)/14=0.0035 mol, hence 0.21 g propan-2-ol.

  3. C aniline rapidly gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline with bromine water
  4. D conversion to acetanilide reduces amino-group activation
Answer and explanation

B. an aryl diazonium salt gives aryl chloride or bromide using copper powder and acid

Gattermann reaction is an aryl diazonium salt gives aryl chloride or bromide using copper powder and acid. Nitrogen is displaced.

JEE-CHEM-1960 · Class XII · Medium

Starting with 0.022 mol substrate, aniline is diazotised with NaNO₂/HCl at 273–278 K; the diazonium solution is then warmed with water. The stated target product is recovered in 83% overall molar yield relative to its stoichiometric maximum. Find the mass of phenol. Use C=12, H=1, N=14, O=16, Cl=35.5 as needed. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 2.068 g
  2. B 1.71644 g
  3. C 5.14932 g
  4. D 1.99034 g
Answer and explanation

B. 1.71644 g

Diazotisation gives benzenediazonium salt; hydrolysis replaces its diazonium group by OH. The stoichiometric target amount is 1×0.022 mol. Applying the overall yield and M=94 gives 1.71644 g.

JEE-CHEM-2011 · Class XII · Difficult

Peptide residue composition

A pure linear unbranched peptide contains only glycine and alanine residues and has molar mass 829 g mol⁻¹. Complete hydrolysis gives 13 mol total amino acids per mole of peptide.   3. C 16.352201 mL
  4. D 24.528302 mL

JEE-CHEM-2043 · Class XII · Medium

Neutralisation calorimetry

Equal volumes of dilute HCl and NaOH solutions at the same initial temperature are mixed in an insulated calorimeter, and the temperature rises. Neglect heat loss and calorimeter heat capacity. Which combined inference is correct?

  1. A No heat is exchanged between reaction and solution
  2. B The solution loses heat; the reaction has negative ΔH
  3. C The solution gains heat; the neutralisation reaction has negative ΔH
  4. D The solution gains heat; the reaction has positive ΔH
Answer and explanation

C. The solution gains heat; the neutralisation reaction has negative ΔH

q_solution=mcΔT is positive. At constant pressure q_reaction=−q_solution, so the strong-acid/strong-base neutralisation is exothermic.

A 0.44 g sample containing 67% anhydrous Na₂CO₃ and nonreactive impurities is dissolved. What volume of 0.100 M HCl completely converts its carbonate to CO₂? M(Na₂CO₃)=106 g mol⁻¹. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 27.811321 mL
  2. B 83.018868 mL
  3. C 166.86792 mL
  4. D 55.622642 mL

D. 55.622642 mL

Pure carbonate amount=mass×purity/106. Complete neutralisation requires twice that HCl amount. Divide by 0.100 mol L⁻¹ and convert to mL: 55.622642.

  3. C 0.027160494 mol L⁻¹
  4. D 0.040740741 mol L⁻¹

A. 0.081481481 mol L⁻¹

JEE-CHEM-2063 · Class XII · Easy

carbylamine test

Which description best identifies carbylamine test?

  1. A a versatile aromatic intermediate
  2. B benzenesulfonyl chloride distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary amines
  3. C primary amines form foul-smelling isocyanides with chloroform and alcoholic KOH
  4. D a primary aromatic amine forms a diazonium salt with nitrous acid at 0 to 5 degrees Celsius
Answer and explanation

C. primary amines form foul-smelling isocyanides with chloroform and alcoholic KOH

Carbylamine test is primary amines form foul-smelling isocyanides with chloroform and alcoholic KOH. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond.

  1. A 1.1883 g
  2. B 1.5844 g
  3. C 0.7922 g
  4. D 0.3961 g

D. 0.3961 g

K₂SO₄ supplies one sulfate for two K⁺. Thus sulfate amount=n(K⁺)/2, and BaSO₄ mass=233n/2=0.3961 g.

JEE-CHEM-2065 · Class XI · Easy

enthalpy of solution

If dissolving a salt raises the calorimeter temperature, the dissolution process under those conditions is:

  1. A endothermic with positive enthalpy of solution
  2. B exothermic with negative enthalpy of solution
  3. C athermal
  4. D necessarily reversible
Answer and explanation

B. exothermic with negative enthalpy of solution

A temperature rise shows heat release by the dissolution process to the calorimetric contents.

JEE-CHEM-2066 · Class XI · Easy

good laboratory practice

For good laboratory practice, which laboratory practice is correct?

  1. A Add water rapidly to concentrated acid while heating the mixture in a closed vessel.
  2. B Add water rapidly to concentrated acid.
  3. C When diluting concentrated acid, add acid slowly to water with stirring.
  4. D Seal the hot mixture immediately.
Answer and explanation

C. When diluting concentrated acid, add acid slowly to water with stirring.

The controlled addition dissipates heat and reduces splashing.

JEE-CHEM-2067 · Class XII · Easy

Lucas test

Which description best identifies Lucas test?

  1. A controlled oxidation gives an aldehyde and further oxidation gives a carboxylic acid
  2. B mild oxidants do not oxidize it readily because the carbinol carbon lacks hydrogen
  3. C oxidation gives a ketone
  4. D a test distinguishing classes of alcohols using concentrated HCl and ZnCl₂
Answer and explanation

D. a test distinguishing classes of alcohols using concentrated HCl and ZnCl₂

Lucas test is a test distinguishing classes of alcohols using concentrated HCl and ZnCl₂. Tertiary alcohols give turbidity fastest.

JEE-CHEM-2125 · Class XII · Medium

For the initial-rate study of iodide oxidation by hydrogen peroxide in acidic solution, doubling [I⁻] alone doubles the initial rate and doubling [H₂O₂] alone doubles it. Acidity and temperature remain fixed. What rate law and change follow if both concentrations are doubled?

  1. A r=k[I⁻][H₂O₂]; rate becomes twice as large
  2. B r=k[I⁻]²; rate becomes twice as large
  3. C r=k[H₂O₂] only; rate is unchanged
  4. D r=k[I⁻][H₂O₂]; rate becomes four times as large
Answer and explanation

D. r=k[I⁻][H₂O₂]; rate becomes four times as large

The separate concentration changes establish first order in each reactant under the fixed conditions. Doubling both multiplies the initial rate by 2×2=4.

Anhydrous CuSO₄ dissolves in water in an insulated calorimeter. The measured solution temperature rises. Neglect heat loss and calorimeter heat capacity. Which pair describes the solution heat and molar enthalpy of dissolution?

  1. A q_solution<0; ΔH_solution=−q_solution/n(CuSO₄)
  2. B q_solution=0; ΔH_solution must be zero
  3. C q_solution>0; ΔH_solution=−q_solution/n(CuSO₄)
  4. D q_solution>0; ΔH_solution=+q_solution/n(CuSO₄)

The warming solution gains sensible heat. Energy conservation assigns the opposite heat to dissolution, and division by the amount dissolved gives the negative molar enthalpy.

JEE-CHEM-2153 · Class XI · Medium

Acid–base titration concentration

20 mL HCl of concentration 0.155 M requires 36 mL NaOH solution for exact neutralisation. What is the NaOH concentration? Assume the endpoint equals equivalence. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.086111111 mol L⁻¹
  2. B 0.25833333 mol L⁻¹
  3. C 0.043055556 mol L⁻¹
  4. D 0.155 mol L⁻¹
Answer and explanation

A. 0.086111111 mol L⁻¹

HCl and NaOH react 1:1. Conserving reacted moles gives CB=CA VA/VB=0.086111111 M.

JEE-CHEM-2154 · Class XI · Medium

Barium and sulfate confirmatory stoichiometry

A neutral sample contains 0.0052 mol K⁺ solely as K₂SO₄. On adding excess BaCl₂, all sulfate precipitates as BaSO₄. Find dry precipitate mass. M(BaSO₄)=233 g mol⁻¹. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.3029 g
  2. B 0.6058 g
  3. C 1.2116 g
  4. D 0.3562 g
Answer and explanation

B. 0.6058 g

K₂SO₄ supplies one sulfate for two K⁺. Thus sulfate amount=n(K⁺)/2, and BaSO₄ mass=233n/2=0.6058 g.

JEE-CHEM-2155 · Class XII · Medium

Acetanilide preparation and yield

0.024 mol aniline is acetylated with excess acetic anhydride to prepare acetanilide. After purification, the isolated yield is 84%. Find product mass. Product formula C₈H₉NO; C=12, H=1, N=14, O=16. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.9072 g
  2. B 1.3608 g
  3. C 2.35872 g
  4. D 2.7216 g
Answer and explanation

D. 2.7216 g

One aniline molecule gives one acetanilide molecule. M=135; isolated mass=135n×yield=2.7216 g.

JEE-CHEM-2156 · Class XI · Easy

Qualitative salt analysis: S²⁻

Acid treatment releases a gas that blackens moist lead acetate paper. Which ion is indicated?

  1. A Cl⁻
  2. B NO₃⁻
  3. C S²⁻
  4. D SO₄²⁻
Answer and explanation

C. S²⁻

H₂S gives black PbS with lead(II) acetate.

JEE-CHEM-2157 · Class XII · Easy

Tollens test

Which description best identifies Tollens test?

  1. A aldehydes reduce diamminesilver(I) to metallic silver
  2. B many aliphatic aldehydes reduce Cu²⁺ to brick-red Cu₂O
  3. C a carbonyl group is reduced to methylene using zinc amalgam and hydrochloric acid
  4. D methyl ketones and compounds oxidizable to them give yellow CHI₃
Answer and explanation

A. aldehydes reduce diamminesilver(I) to metallic silver

Tollens test is aldehydes reduce diamminesilver(I) to metallic silver. Most ketones do not give the silver mirror.

JEE-CHEM-2158 · Class XI · Easy

2,4-DNP test

Which description best identifies 2,4-DNP test?

  1. A methyl ketones and compounds oxidizable to them give yellow CHI₃
  2. B many aliphatic aldehydes reduce Cu²⁺ to brick-red Cu₂O
  3. C aldehydes and ketones give yellow or orange hydrazone precipitates
  4. D aldehydes reduce diamminesilver(I) to metallic silver
Answer and explanation

C. aldehydes and ketones give yellow or orange hydrazone precipitates

2,4-dnp test is aldehydes and ketones give yellow or orange hydrazone precipitates. The test detects a carbonyl group.

JEE-CHEM-2159 · Class XI · Easy

Qualitative salt analysis: Mg²⁺

After interfering cations have been removed, an ammoniacal solution buffered with NH₄Cl gives white crystalline MgNH₄PO₄ with phosphate. Which ion is indicated?

  1. A Cu²⁺
  2. B Fe³⁺
  3. C Ba²⁺
  4. D Mg²⁺
Answer and explanation

D. Mg²⁺

The ammonium magnesium phosphate precipitate confirms magnesium under these conditions.

JEE-CHEM-2160 · Class XI · Medium

Aluminium hydroxide precipitation

A solution contains 0.0073 mol chloride ions solely from completely dissociated AlCl₃. Ammonia solution precipitates all aluminium as Al(OH)₃ without excess-alkali dissolution. Find precipitate mass. Al=27, O=16, H=1. Choose the closest listed value.

  1. A 0.5694 g
  2. B 0.1898 g
  3. C 0.3796 g
  4. D 0.063266667 g
Answer and explanation

B. 0.1898 g

One Al³⁺ corresponds to three Cl⁻. The precipitate amount is n(Cl⁻)/3; M[Al(OH)₃]=78, giving 0.1898 g.
